summary: Inspect and operate Tether, the per-user session daemon that owns Aico and A-Term tmux sessions.

help:
Usage: st tether [--instance NAME] [--json] <command>

Forwards to Tether's own CLI (`tether`), which talks to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tether/<instance>/control.sock.

Commands:
  doctor                        check host prerequisites and the running daemon
  version                       print the CLI and daemon versions
  sessions [list | get <id>]    session catalog
  sessions new [--tool T] [--project P] [--name N]
  sessions end <id>             retire one session (reads its generation first)
  sessions attach <id>          print the exact tmux attach argv
  sessions diagnostics <id>
  legacy [list | end <name>]    A-Term summitflow-<uuid> sessions (attach/end only)
  roots [list | show <requestId>]
  tools [list | get <slug>]     merged agent-tool registry (add/default/enable/disable/rm mutate it)
  projects [--refresh]          project list (SummitFlow, else local)

The instance defaults to $TETHER_INSTANCE or "default". The daemon is never started by this command; `serve` and `import-aico` belong to the tether@<instance>.service unit and the cutover procedure. Fleet roots: prefer st sessions start/close so the fleet ledger records them.

usage.when: inspect Tether-owned sessions, roots, agent tools or daemon health, or end one exact session
precautions: Ending a session is an exact generation-fenced retirement; an ended session is never resurrected. Fleet roots: use st sessions close.
tools add/default/enable/disable/rm change launches in both Aico and A-Term.
Never starts the daemon; when tether@<instance>.service is down commands report it unavailable.
